newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar hits fresh 48-month high vs yen in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar hits fresh 48-month high vs yen in Tokyo.

text.p: The dollar briefly rose above 124.75 yen in afternoon Tokyo trade on Friday, propelled to a fresh four-year high by continuing rallies in U.S. asset prices, dealers said.
The dollar rose as high as 124.78 yen, they added.

Fresh gains in U.S. stocks and bonds in New York trading overnight fuelled bullish sentiment on the dollar, although there were lingering fears of dollar-selling intervention by the Bank of Japan (BOJ) above 125 yen, they added.

The dollar stood at around 124.68/78 yen at 0655 GMT, after rising to about 124.82. Dealers said the dollar powered higher against the yen despite a lack of fresh factors in late trade, although dollar buying interest had been strong since early trading here after a rally in U.S. stocks on Thursday.
"Although the dollar hit a fresh high, its rise has been gradual because of continued concerns over (possible Bank of Japan) intervention," said a Japanese bank dealer.
He said the greenback was likely to reach the psychologically key 125 yen level in the near term.
